title: A Slipshod Resurrection
text: “You sure do love to chat and gossip, huh… so, how’d it go?”
Half exasperated, Arc scratched his cheek and started washing his back with a towel.
“For some reason, he wouldn’t tell me anything clearly, saying I’d find out later if I touched his back.”
“Hmm. Sounds like you were trying to steer him into letting you wash his back.”
Arc answered with an expression that, for some reason, I felt didn’t quite match the truth.
“Shall I wash your back, then?”
“Sure, I’ll take you up on that. Motoyasu-kun.”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
I washed Arc’s back for him. There were no particular issues to speak of.
“Thanks, Motoyasu-kun. My turn now.”
And so he washed mine in return. Afterward, we soaked in the large bath together. Come to think of it, Arc had apparently experienced peeping battles in another world before.
“I wonder if Big Sister and the others have finished bathing yet—should be about time.”

It was time for me to act, to elevate the charm of the Filolial-samas who had entered the women’s bath. I rose from the tub with a splash and casually approached the wall separating the two baths. What method should I use this time? Drilling a hole in the wall, phasing through it to peek… even if I phased through, circling around to peek was also an option. Sticking to the ceiling had its merits too… but peering in from the bath side was also a valid approach.
“Paradise lies beyond this wall, I say. Shall we attempt a peek together with Ho-kun next time?”
Among the Filolial-samas, there were some willing to cooperate. Black Thunder was one such example.
“Will Black Thunder be joining as well?”
“Yeah! Where do we look from?”
Black Thunder was quite the good sport.
“Wow… that confident stride just leaves me speechless.”
“Hey, hey, Arc-san, you’re neither one nor the other, right? Why don’t you go in over there?”
“Yeah, yeah!”
“Well, you see, someone like me causes trouble if I go into the women’s bath. So it’s simplest to just stick with the men’s side.”
“Hmm.”
“Really? Cats don’t have male or female, so no mating and stuff—that sounds rough.”
“So you can’t even make a special someone even if you wanted to.”
The Filolial-samas seemed to be pitying Arc.
“Ah, but with my mouth, I could—”
Since one of the Filolial-samas uttered a word that really ought to be self-censored, I consciously converted it into a beep.
“Hmm… what open kids you are—Filolials really are like this. Come to think of it, they all really do resemble their ancestor.”

Arc gave a troubled, wry smile. Ancestor… since he came from far in the past, he would know, I supposed. Anyway, right now, peeping was the priority. And so, the moment I touched the wall—BAM! An impact shot through the spot where my hand made contact. It was the sound of a warning that any further intrusion would be met with armed retaliation. Ngh… it seemed Big Sister and the others were still bathing.
“Hey…”
“It seems Big Sister and the others are present. First, let’s change our approach. We’ll phase through the ceiling and peek from above, Black Thunder!”
“O-okay.”
“Hmm. If he ever meets that guy, they’d probably hit it off great. Well, Naofumi-kun and Raphtalia-chan and her are the ones who’d probably suffer for it, though.”
Later, Arc apparently warned that if I got a proper girlfriend, he’d want me to stop this sort of thing.
“Well, I’ll be heading up and cooling off now, so see you later.”
Oh dear. Arc, just like Father, wasn’t much for company either.
“Dewa! I say!”

I grabbed Black Thunder and phased through the ceiling, carrying out my peeping mission from above the women’s bath. To cut to the result: we were thwarted by Big Sister and the others and failed, ending up subjected to a stern lecture alongside Black Thunder afterward. Big Sister’s defenses truly were ironclad, I must say. It was absolutely terrifying, I tell you.

It was one day, right as evening was setting in. Trash arrived together with the Queen at Father’s place and headed into Doctor’s research lab. I was busy pestering a lonely Ho-kun when suddenly Arc appeared out of nowhere, as if he’d used a Portal.
“Hm? What’s up?”
“Ah, well. There’s a matter better suited to you, so I came to fetch you.”
“Ehh… something that needs me?”
Ho-kun responded to Arc’s words with obvious reluctance.
“You don’t have to be so blunt about it.”
“Well, sure, but—so what do you want me to do? What’s the payment?”
“I’m in a good mood, so I won’t demand payment for something this minor. So greedy.”
“Boo.”
Ho-kun uttered the exact line Filolial-samas say when protesting. Let’s protest together, then.
“Boo, I say.”
“No, I was just mimicking the Filolials here—you don’t need to copy me too… fine, fine. I get it. I’ll go, right?”
“It’s over there, then.”
Resigned, Ho-kun pointed toward the lab Arc had indicated, sighing all the while. I followed after Ho-kun.
“Why are you tagging along?”
“To burn the sight of Ho-kun’s heroics into my eyes, I say.”
“Seriously, you never change… I really do feel, deep in my heart, that I mishandled our first meeting.”
Muttering something like that, Ho-kun walked on looking utterly resigned.
“Why walk when you could just fly?”
“What’s the point of flying such a short distance? Walking’s fine.”
“Kweh, kweh, I say.”
“You too, seriously… haah.”
For some reason, Ho-kun’s steps were heavy. And so, when we arrived at the lab, there were Father and the others, along with Trash and Fiancée. And the Queen was seated in a chair.
“That cat over there called me—what do you need?”
“Ah, we were doing the Queen’s regular checkup when Arc said you were perfect for it and went to fetch you…”
“You can tell just by looking, can’t you?”
“Well… I can tell from the faint smell of something starting to fester, at least.”
From Arc’s explanation, it seemed Ho-kun had grasped the situation.
“Ho-kun, please explain it to me, I say!”
“Yeah, yeah. Seems like Motoyasu-kun doesn’t get it, so I guess I’ll explain. That person there was resurrected through some pretty slipshod method, wasn’t she?”

Come to think of it, the Queen had once been killed by Takt through the Crimson Swine’s machinations, then revived by the power of the Crimson Swine’s true body. I’d heard that Trash’s efforts had broken the brainwashing afterward.
“Indeed…”
Trash nodded, uncharacteristically subdued.
“So you’re the ones I’ve heard about. P-pleased to meet you.”
“Well… I suppose that’s how it turns out if this timeline continues as is. Best to avoid altering the past based on this axis…”
Ho-kun muttered, glancing repeatedly at the Queen.
“In other words, you want me to handle it.”
“That’s right.”
Arc nodded at Ho-kun’s question. Oh-ho! This was shaping up to be a moment where Ho-kun would truly shine!
“Do your best, Ho-kun, I say!”
“Never mind Motoyasu-kun—you’re trying to conveniently use me here…”
“You’re better suited for this than I am.”

“I guess that’s true, but still. Ugh, fine. Let me explain to everyone here, including Motoyasu-kun. That person there was resurrected through an extremely sloppy method—her body’s fine, like a reincarnator’s, but worse than just having a rotten soul. Actually, her soul’s condition is fine if treated properly. Seems her original will was good.”
“So the soul isn’t a problem, then?”

“Not that it’s no problem, just that if handled properly, it’ll still be fine. Like, a hand that’s festering and rotting, but if you cut away the bad part, it can still heal. There are people out there whose souls have rotted without even reincarnating, but I judged that hers is still salvageable.”
Ohh… so it seemed the state of the Queen’s soul was actually good. Being resurrected by the Crimson Swine’s true body must have been that agonizing an ordeal.
“Phoenix, Slayer of Gods. Please, save my wife…”
Trash bowed his head deeply.

“Yeah, yeah. You all defeated the mastermind after a long, painful battle. I’ll do it free of charge, so don’t make such a bothersome request out of it. If you keep bowing that deeply, I might just start asking for payment.”
Ho-kun grumbled about how being treated like a god was such a hassle.
“There are worlds out there where the natural law permits resurrection of the dead, but the laws governing souls differ between that world and this one.”
“In games and such, there’s resurrection magic… I suppose that tracks. Bringing back the dead really is more of a fantasy in reality, but knowing that guy did it, of course it’d be slipshod.”
Father seemed to understand as well. Indeed, in games, resurrecting the dead was practically taken for granted.
